issues.legal_issue: A provision of residence for a Hindu widow can form part of maintenance owed to her.
material_facts: The widow had a pre-existing right to maintenance as the widow of a deceased coparcener.
An arbitration agreement referred to allotting property and money to her for residence and maintenance for life.
The award gave her a choice between two properties for residence and varied the accompanying lump-sum payment according to her choice.
issues.conclusion: Maintenance necessarily includes provision for residence, and it may be provided through a residence for the widow’s lifetime as well as money for other necessary expenditure.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the understanding of maintenance reflected in pre-Act Hindu law, including the widow’s entitlement to reside in the family dwelling house, and Section 3(d) of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, which defines maintenance to include residence.

predicates.female_maintenance_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a female Hindu’s provision for maintenance.
predicates.pre_existing_maintenance_entitlement: The woman had a right to maintenance before the arrangement providing for her support.
predicates.residence_provided_as_part_of_settlement: The arrangement providing for her support included a place for her to reside.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns a female Hindu’s maintenance, she had a prior maintenance entitlement, and her support arrangement included a place to reside, the residence is part of that maintenance.

issues.legal_issue: A limited interest in property given to a Hindu woman in lieu of her pre-existing right to maintenance becomes full ownership when she possesses the property at the commencement of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.
material_facts: The arbitration reference recognised the widow’s pre-existing right to maintenance and provided for both property and money in settlement of that right.
The award gave her the right to reside in and use the chosen property for life, make certain changes and repairs, and prohibited her from transferring or damaging it.
She chose the Bidasar property and took possession of it under a document confirming her right to reside there and use it.
She possessed the property when the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 came into force.
She later executed sale deeds for parts of the property’s nohra.
issues.conclusion: The widow acquired limited ownership rights in the property in recognition of her pre-existing right to maintenance; those rights became full ownership under Section 14(1), and she was entitled to sell the nohra. Section 14(2) did not prevent that result because the property was provided in satisfaction of a pre-existing right, not acquired for the first time without such a right.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, and its Explanation broadly cover property possessed by a female Hindu and acquired in lieu of maintenance; Section 14(2) is confined to property acquired for the first time without a pre-existing right under an instrument prescribing a restricted estate. Under V. Tulasamma v. V. Sesha Reddi, property allotted in satisfaction of a widow’s pre-existing maintenance right is not a first-time grant. Smt. Gulwant Kaur v. Mohinder Singh, Badri Pershad v. Smt. Kanso Devi, and Bai Vajia v. Thakorbhai Chelabhai support the requirement of a lawful vestige of title and the enlargement of a limited interest. Eramma v. Veerupana and Mangal Singh v. Smt. Rattno establish that mere possession without title is insufficient; they do not exclude an interest arising from a pre-existing maintenance right.

rule.if: female_property_conversion_case and pre_existing_maintenance_right and property_given_in_lieu_of_maintenance and possessed_at_reform_commencement and restricted_lifetime_interest

predicates.female_property_conversion_case: The proceeding concerns whether a female Hindu’s property interest became full ownership under a change in succession law.
predicates.pre_existing_maintenance_right: The woman had a right to maintenance before the arrangement that provided her with property.
predicates.property_given_in_lieu_of_maintenance: The arrangement provided the property to the woman in satisfaction of her maintenance right.
predicates.possessed_at_reform_commencement: The woman possessed the property when the relevant succession reform came into force.
predicates.restricted_lifetime_interest: The arrangement limited the woman’s interest to her lifetime and restricted her power to transfer the property.

issues.definition: In a female property-conversion proceeding, if a woman had a prior maintenance right, received property in satisfaction of it, possessed the property when the reform commenced, and held only a restricted lifetime interest, she has full ownership and transfer power.
